rationale: The verse opens the second Solomonic collection with the skeleton-initial phrase גַּם אֵ֭לֶּה (oshb:Prov.25.1) ("also these"), the second of exactly two verse-initial gam-elleh sites in the book (the other, outside this part, is 24:23), and carries the interior word מִשְׁלֵ֣י (oshb:Prov.25.1) ("proverbs of"), one of exactly three mishle-anywhere sites (1:1, 10:1 verse-initial; 25:1 interior). rationale: The two verses share the exact skeleton token מְ֝לָכִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.25.2) / מְ֝לָכִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.25.3) ("kings", plural) and the root חקר ("search"), realized as the infinitive חֲקֹ֣ר (oshb:Prov.25.2) in v2 and the noun חֵֽקֶר (oshb:Prov.25.3) in v3. v2 states the principle that kings' matters are for searching out; v3 supplies the illustration (heaven's height, earth's depth) that makes the kings' heart categorically unsearchable. A targeted sweep of this part's skeletons finds the plural form at 2 of the part's 83 verses (25:2 and 25:3), distinct from the singular used of the historical king in 25:1, 25:5, 25:6.
